children: Australian financial markets are pricing in 1.5 more interest rate increases, something that feels aggressive, says Andrew Canobi, director of fixed income at Franklin Templeton Australia. Three-year government bonds at these levels look attractive, he adds. The challenge the market has is that restrictive policy is already showing up in the data, leaving the RBA in a bind. It's likely employment will cool from here and broader inflation pressures will ease. If the RBA does hike again in coming meetings, the market could try and embrace the possibility of easings into 2027, he adds. (james.glynn@wsj.com; X @JamesGlynnWSJ)
